new_jobs.title: PROJECT MANAGER-Automated Synthesis Facility
new_jobs.description:
ABOUT US:

Scripps Research is a nonprofit biomedical institute ranked as one of the most influential in the world for its impact on innovation. We celebrated our 100-year legacy in 2024. This significant milestone marks a century of seminal discoveries in immunology, infectious diseases (such as COVID-19, flu, HIV), neuroscience, heart disease, cancer, and more. Located in La Jolla, California, the institute houses six research departments, multiple Nobel laureates, a top-ranked graduate school and a leading postdoctoral training program. Scripps Research encompasses two elite and highly innovative institutes, the Calibr-Skaggs Institute for Innovative Medicines and Scripps Research Translational Institute, which merge foundational studies in biology, chemistry and computer science with translational science to produce pioneering drugs and advances in digital and precision medicine. Together, we cultivate new scientific leaders and expand the frontiers of knowledge to deliver medical breakthroughs impacting human health around the globe. If you have a passion for making a difference, this could be your opportunity to join our transformative team.
POSITION TITLE:
 Project Manager
POSITION SUMMARY: 

The Automated Synthesis Facility (ASF) at Scripps Research hosts the Chemistry Node of the U.S. National Science Foundation Programmable Cloud Laboratory (PCL) Test Bed, a four-year NSF Cooperative Agreement. The Node is turning ASF from a supervised shared-use facility into a remotely accessible, closed-loop, AI-driven chemistry platform: instruments exposed through open standardized interfaces, experiments planned and refined by machine-learning models, and results captured against FAIR-compliant metadata schemas. The work spans three institutions: Scripps Research, UCLA, and Sunthetics, Inc. with several institutional and industrial partners.
We are looking for a full-time Project Manager to serve as the Node’s dedicated project management professional. Working with the Principal Investigator/Node Director, the Project Manager assists in managing the budget, schedule, and scope of the award; drives the Node against NSF’s fixed implementation gates; leads reporting to NSF; and coordinates the Node’s role in Test Bed-wide governance, standards development, and user recruitment. The position is named Node-level Key Personnel under the award’s Cooperative Agreement Programmatic Terms and Conditions and sits on the Node Management Team. The role is a fixture of both operations: approximately 90% of effort supports the NSF award, with the balance supporting day-to-day administration of the Automated Synthesis Facility.
DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITES:

Assist the Node Director in managing the budget, schedule, and scope of the project, including expenditures against the approved budget, subaward invoicing and deliverables (UCLA; Sunthetics, Inc.), and coordination with the Scripps’ Office of Sponsored Programs and financial teams.
Maintain the Strategic Implementation Plan and Project Execution Plan (PEP) as living documents and keep the Instrument Inventory Table current in a form satisfying 2 CFR §200.313 equipment use requirements.
Drive execution against the PCL Implementation Timeline — Alpha (≤12 months), Beta (≤18 months), Robust User Service (≤24 months), and Post-Award Continued Operation (≤48 months) — maintaining the Node risk register and surfacing schedule risk early for re-planning with the Node Director.
Lead reporting to NSF: quarterly project reports (quarterly in year one, thereafter as requested by the cognizant Program Officer) plus annual and final reports via Research.gov, covering timeline progress, cross-node standards, workshop outcomes and user onboarding, research security and safety, and data and AI operations.
Provide project management support to the Node Executive Committee and the three Technical Integration Working Groups: set agendas, coordinate the biweekly integration and Science Driver meetings and the monthly all-hands, and track decisions and action items to closure.
Coordinate instrumentation procurement, installation, and vendor engineering engagements with the Node Director, vendor project teams, ASF staff, and institutional Facilities and Environmental Health & Safety.
Coordinate cross-node and NSF-facing engagement: Test Bed working groups on protocols, instrument validation, metadata standards, and AI model practices; site and reverse-site reviews; and the annual in-person PCL PI meeting, including logistics for the meeting the Node hosts.
Facilitate communication across a distributed technical team — ASF staff, academic co-Investigators, industrial AI/ML engineers, and instrument vendors — and between the Node, its users, and the cognizant NSF Program Officer.
Coordinate Recruitment and On-Boarding Workshops and the user-access pipeline, including solicitation, the feasibility and alignment review with the User Access Committee, and tracking of safety, export-control, and responsible-AI onboarding requirements.
Track and report Node metrics — operational robustness, scientific impact, and structured user-satisfaction surveys — maintain the response strategy for user requests and run the quarterly continuous-improvement cycle.
Support compliance and administrative requirements of the Cooperative Agreement, including Key Personnel prior-approval notifications, participant-support cost handling, Build America Buy America and CHIPS and Science Act §10636 provisions, Bayh-Dole and knowledge-sharing agreements, and NSF acknowledgement and brand standards.
Maintain project documentation and version-controlled records and keep current the Node’s public-facing information on capabilities, onboarding, reproducibility practices, and training materials.
ASF facility administration (approximately 10% of effort).
Support day-to-day operation of the Automated Synthesis Facility alongside the Node: user billing and recharge through Idea Elan Infinity, purchase-order reconciliation and laboratory ordering, travel coordination for the ASF/Node Director, and correspondence with ASF external partners and service clients.

REQUIREMENTS:

Bachelor’s degree in chemistry, Biology, Engineering, Computer Science, Information Systems, or related field.
Project Management Professional (PMP) certification, or equivalent qualification , as required by the award’s Cooperative Agreement Programmatic Terms and Conditions.
Minimum of four years’ experience in project management and/or leadership, coordinating scientists and engineers to develop technical solutions to scientific problems.
Demonstrated experience managing budget, schedule, and scope on a multi-institutional project, tracking deliverables, progress, and metrics against a defined roadmap and work plan.
Demonstrated experience working with a diverse set of colleagues, including chemists, engineers, and data scientists with a variety of backgrounds.
Strategic and analytical thinking.
Strong oral and written communications skills coupled with effective interpersonal and collaboration skills.

PREFERED SKILLSTET:

An advanced degree (Master’s or Ph.D.) in a scientific or engineering domain.
Experience working with federally-funded research, particularly NSF cooperative agreements or center- and facility-scale awards, including Research.gov reporting, subaward administration, and prior-approval processes.
Familiarity with synthetic or analytical chemistry, high-throughput experimentation, laboratory automation, or shared research-instrumentation facilities.
Working familiarity with instrument APIs, FAIR data and metadata standards, and AI/ML-assisted experimentation.
Experience supporting research security, export control, or laboratory safety programs.
Experience organizing workshops, training programs, or user-facility onboarding.
Experience mentoring others.
Proactiveness, to identify potential issues and develop preemptive solutions.
Experience with core-facility recharge and billing platforms (e.g., Idea Elan Infinity) and with institutional purchasing, purchase-order reconciliation, and travel reimbursement workflows.

LOCATION:
La Jolla, California. This position is on-site at the Scripps Research California campus and requires regular in-person presence in the Automated Synthesis Facility. Periodic travel is required for partner-site engagement, NSF-organized meetings and workshops, and the annual in-person PCL PI meeting. 
PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS:
This position works in an office environment with regular presence in an active laboratory environment. Further details of the physical requirements of established essential functions for this position will be addressed/discussed during the interview process.
COMPENSATION:
The expected hiring range for this position is $77,200 to $96,500 per year, commensurate with experience. Consideration will be given to experience that exceeds the listed requirements.
COMPREHENSIVE BENEFITS INCLUDE:

Employer Contributed Retirement Plan - Depending on eligibility, employees receive an employer contributed retirement plan (no employee contribution required) and the option to contribute to a 403(b) (which is similar to a 401(k) using your own pre or post-tax dollars)
Full Suite of Health and Welfare plans including three medical plan options (including an HSA available option), dental, vision, life insurance, disability, EAP and more
Access to Flexible Spending Accounts (Medical/Dependent Care)
Competitive vacation and sick leave policies
Free, on-site parking

We are seeking an experienced Project Manager to partner with technology leaders in organizing, governing, and advancing highly visible ServiceNow initiatives. This role will provide structure and delivery discipline across Continuous Improvement & Acceleration, Strategic Governance, platform initiatives, and the associated portfolio of work.
The Project Manager will serve as a connector between leaders, delivery teams, business stakeholders, and partners, ensuring priorities are clear, commitments are tracked, risks and decisions are surfaced early, and leadership has a consistent view of progress and business value.

The Project Manager will work with initiative owners to translate detailed platform activity, backlog progress, dependencies, risks, metrics, and accomplishments into concise, decision-ready materials for senior executives and governance forums.

Key Responsibilities

Strategic Initiative & Delivery Management

Provide project management leadership across high-visibility ServiceNow strategic initiatives and continuous-improvement efforts.
Establish clear objectives, milestones, deliverables, owners, dependencies, and expected outcomes.
Translate broad leadership objectives into actionable work plans and maintain visibility from strategy through execution.
Maintain an integrated view across multiple ServiceNow initiatives rather than managing each effort in isolation.
Facilitate working sessions that move teams from discussion toward clear outcomes, owners, actions, and decisions.
Identify delivery gaps, unclear ownership, competing priorities, and dependencies requiring leadership attention.
Drive follow-through and accountability for committed actions and objectives.

Backlog, Prioritization & Continuous Improvement

Help leaders organize and maintain the strategic initiative and continuous-improvement backlog.
Establish visibility into what is committed, in progress, blocked, and recommended for prioritization next.
Partner with initiative owners to define measurable outcomes and determine when work is complete.
Connect backlog items to strategic priorities, expected value, dependencies, risks, and leadership decisions.
Support prioritization discussions when capacity or competing initiatives require tradeoffs.
Maintain action and decision tracking so governance commitments translate into execution.

Executive Governance & Reporting

Coordinate preparation for recurring executive governance and leadership reviews.
Develop and maintain concise, executive-ready status materials with ServiceNow leaders and subject-matter experts.
Translate complex technical and operational information into clear narratives focused on business value, delivery progress, milestones, risks, dependencies, decisions required, backlog priorities, and measurable outcomes.
Establish a structured preparation cadence for content collection, owner alignment, quality review, and presenter readiness.
Work with presenters to ensure ownership of content and readiness to communicate decisions, risks, and outcomes.

Stakeholder & Leadership Partnership

Build trusted working relationships with ServiceNow platform leadership, managers, technical SMEs, business stakeholders, vendors, and enterprise partners.
Coordinate across teams where work spans organizational or platform boundaries.
Ensure subject-matter experts remain accountable for their content and outcomes while the Project Manager provides the structure that keeps the overall effort moving.
Facilitate alignment when teams have different priorities, perspectives, or definitions of success.
Distinguish issues requiring working-team resolution from those requiring leadership escalation or governance decisions.
Bring the appropriate stakeholders together to resolve cross-functional dependencies.

Risk, Decision & Dependency Management

Maintain visibility into material risks, issues, dependencies, decisions, and actions across assigned initiatives.
Ensure each material item has clear ownership, impact, target resolution, and escalation path.
Surface potential delivery or governance concerns early rather than waiting for executive reporting cycles.
Prepare leadership with the context and options necessary to make decisions.
Track decisions through completion and ensure resulting actions are reflected in plans and backlogs.

What Success Looks Like

The successful Project Manager will establish an operating rhythm where:
Leaders have one reliable view of priorities, progress, backlog, risks, and decisions.
Initiative owners understand their commitments and are prepared for governance discussions.
Executive materials tell a concise business story rather than simply reporting activity.
Metrics and value statements are supportable before reaching senior leadership.
Cross-functional dependencies are surfaced early.
Decisions from governance meetings translate into owned actions.
Continuous-improvement work remains organized and visible as priorities evolve.
ServiceNow leaders can focus on leading the platform and making decisions while the Project Manager provides coordination and delivery structure.

Desired Qualifications

Preferred Experience

Demonstrated project or program management experience supporting complex, highly visible technology initiatives.
Experience working directly with senior leaders and translating detailed delivery information into executive-level communication.
Strong experience establishing governance cadences, project controls, status reporting, backlog visibility, and accountability mechanisms.
Experience coordinating initiatives across multiple technical and business teams.
Demonstrated ability to organize work into clear plans, ownership, milestones, and measurable outcomes.
Strong PowerPoint and executive presentation skills, including the ability to turn technical content into concise leadership narratives.
Experience facilitating working sessions, leadership reviews, and governance meetings.
Strong understanding of RAID management, dependency management, decision tracking, prioritization, and delivery governance.
Familiarity with ServiceNow, ServiceNow platform teams, or enterprise ServiceNow initiatives.
Experience supporting ServiceNow governance, platform modernization, automation, AI/Now Assist, CMDB, Service Mapping, demand management, or similar platform initiatives.
PMP certification.
Experience operating in an Agile, product, portfolio, or hybrid delivery environment.

We’re a bunch of hardworking, fun-loving, people-oriented technology enthusiasts. We love what we do, and we’re passionate about helping our clients thrive in an increasingly complex digital world. Teamwork and collaboration are critical to Zensar’s mission and success, and our teams work on a diverse and challenging mix of technologies across a broad industry spectrum. These industries include banking and financial services, high-tech and manufacturing, healthcare, insurance, retail, and consumer services. Our employees enjoy flexible work arrangements and a competitive benefits package, including medical, dental, vision, 401(k), among other benefits. If you are looking for a place to have an immediate impact, to grow and contribute, where we work hard, play hard, and support each other, consider joining team Zensar!

Zensar is looking for a MDM Business Analyst in the United States (Hybrid). This position is open for Full Time with excellent benefits and professional growth opportunities.

About the Role

MDM requirements

Run on-site discovery and requirements workshops with business and IT stakeholders for in-scope domains such as Customer, Account, Contact and Product.
Document business requirements, user stories and acceptance criteria. Define golden record attributes, data ownership and the systems of record.
Work out business rules for match criteria, trust and survivorship, and hierarchies with the MDM Solution Architect and DQ Analyst.
Prepare source-to-target mappings, attribute-level data dictionaries and business glossary entries.
Maintain the requirements traceability matrix and manage requirement changes through the change control process.

Data stewardship processes

Design end-to-end data stewardship processes: create/update approvals, duplicate review, merge/unmerge decisions and exception handling.
Define steward roles, responsibilities, task queues, SLAs and escalation paths in MDM SaaS.
Document data governance policies, data ownership (RACI) and data standards for mastered entities.
Prepare steward SOPs, process flows and training material. Lead steward onboarding and training sessions.

Salesforce CRM data

Analyze the Salesforce CRM data model: Accounts, Contacts, Leads, Opportunities, record types, account hierarchies, custom objects and fields.
Find Salesforce data quality issues such as duplicates, incomplete records and inconsistent account hierarchies, and define how to fix them.
Define the business rules for syncing golden records back to Salesforce, including field ownership, conflict resolution and duplicate prevention (search-before-create).
Work with the client’s Salesforce admins and sales/service operations teams on process changes after MDM goes live.

Client engagement (onshore)

Act as the main functional contact for client business sponsors, data owners and stewards.
Get timely business sign-offs on requirements, match and survivorship rules, stewardship processes and UAT.
Present requirements, process designs and open decisions in status meetings and steering committees.

Onshore–offshore coordination

Turn client requirements and decisions into clear functional specs for the offshore MDM, CDI, DQ and QA teams.
Run regular overlap calls with the offshore team to clarify requirements and resolve functional questions.
Review offshore deliverables (designs, test cases, UAT scripts) to check they meet business needs.

Testing and go-live support

Help the QA team build test scenarios, and lead UAT planning and execution with business users and data stewards.
Validate match/merge and survivorship outcomes against business expectations.
Support change management, user training, cutover and go-live on site.

Experience:

MDM requirements:
8+ years as a Business Analyst on MDM programs. This must include defining golden record attributes, match/merge and survivorship business rules, hierarchies and source-to-target mappings. Informatica MDM SaaS experience is preferred.
Data stewardship processes:
hands-on experience designing data stewardship workflows, steward roles and SLAs, governance policies and data ownership (RACI) models.
Salesforce CRM data:
strong knowledge of the Salesforce CRM data model (Accounts, Contacts, Leads, account hierarchies, custom objects) and common Salesforce data quality challenges such as duplicates and hierarchy inconsistencies.

Education:

Bachelor’s / Master’s Degree – Information Technology
